children: The Central Bank of Nigeria slashed its key interest rate by 350 bps to 23% during its September 2026 meeting, after keeping it unchanged in July and May.
The decision sought to improve monetary policy transmission, while also supporting economic activity amid moderating inflation and improved foreign exchange stability.
The MPC noted that market rates had diverged from the benchmark lending rate, making the policy less effective.
Meanwhile, the annual inflation rate eased marginally to 15.39% in August 2026 from 15.43% in July, marking the lowest since March and the third straight month of slowdown.
However, recent fuel-price increases could soon reverse the downward trend in inflation.

title: Nigeria Cuts Key Policy Rate to 23%
